items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: Eliza, my ex, she would tell them, “hey, Daddy’s on TV.”

ctx.x: Did they have any idea what you did?

Well they had an idea, you know, they knew I did music. They didn’t really care. Eliza, my ex, she would tell them, “hey, Daddy’s on TV.” And they’d go, “yeah, so, who cares?” You know I remember my daughter coming to like the first concert and falling asleep. Or like I’d come backstage, and there was like one song where I would get a break in the whole show. It’s like a two and a half hour show so I’m standing up there playing the whole thing, and the keyboards and drums are kind of the solid rhythm © Hamilton…

section to keep it all together. It’s not kind of a traditional thing. So it’s very rhythmic keyboard playing so you’re kind of holding things together. And I remember going backstage and like my son’s sound asleep on the couch. So yeah. They didn’t think it was cool until their friends thought it was cool, and then they go, “oh, maybe Dad’s all right.”
